pairs.question: quid putem?
pairs.derivation: Cicero poses and answers his own question. The framing 'si quaeris' ('if you ask') is droppable meta-narration of the asking, leaving the bare interrogative 'quid putem?' Answer is the self-supplied reply 'ego fructum puto.' to the full stop; what follows ('sed quid multa?') turns to a new topic.

pairs.question: quo modo hoc ergo lues?
pairs.answer: Vno scilicet si mihi librum miseris;
pairs.derivation: Cicero asks how Atticus will atone (for hearing Tyrannio without him) and answers himself. Answer cut at the semicolon, which closes the complete operative answer ('by one means only, if you send me the book'); what follows ('quod ut facias etiam atque etiam rogo') turns from answering to a request, so it is omitted.

pairs.question: quid ergo? nihil litterae?
pairs.answer: in hac quidem re vereor ne etiam contra; nam essem fortasse durior.
pairs.derivation: Cicero voices an imagined objection from Atticus and answers it. The framing 'inquies' ('you will say'), which narrates the speaking, is dropped from between the two interrogative fragments; the utterance itself ('quid ergo?' ... 'nihil litterae?') is quoted contiguously around it. Answer runs to the full stop; what follows ('exculto enim animo...') is general elaboration.
